findings.Quote: "I have seven days left on this contract," he said. "Make it easy for me and don't be where I can find you for seven days."
findings.Note: Purpose requires the confrontation to rest on a false premise (stolen data) that Ekow is meant to be enforcing under; but the scene has Ekow already visibly uncertain/doubting the premise ('You should [ask]') before issuing the ultimatum, undercutting the tension of him acting on a false accusation — he seems to be extending a deadline out of professional courtesy despite doubting the charge, which softens rather than dramatizes the false-premise stakes.
findings.Fix: Either have Ekow commit more firmly to the accusation before the deadline, or make explicit that he's giving Seto time BECAUSE of the doubt, so the logic of the seven days is clear.

findings.Quote: He had the quiet of a man raised in rooms built to meet a body correctly at every surface, rooms that had never once been the wrong temperature for him, doors that had never stuck.
findings.Note: Purple metaphor stacking that overexplains the class-signifier point already made; fails as literal image (a room can't 'meet a body correctly at every surface') and tells rather than shows privilege.
findings.Fix: Cut to one concrete image, e.g. 'He had the quiet of someone whose doors had never stuck.'

findings.Quote: The word landed somewhere below her sternum before she'd decided to feel anything — a small tightening, gone before it reached her face.
findings.Note: Somatic dread-marker (word landing below the sternum) is a stock interiority device for suppressed emotion; tells us she felt dread without giving a fresh physical or behavioral specific.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete external action that shows suppression, e.g. she over-grips the cup or miscounts her change.

findings.Quote: There was nothing left to relay that the bleed hadn't already delivered in its own currency.
findings.Note: States the bleed-as-truth-channel thesis directly rather than dramatizing it through specific sensory/emotional detail, undercutting the 'show' half of the beat's purpose.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete instance of what he felt and how it matched her news, without naming the mechanism outright.

findings.Quote: The building read like a building.
findings.Note: purple-flat line trying to sound cryptic/profound but is tautological filler
findings.Fix: cut, or replace with a specific observed detail that carries the irony

findings.Quote: The weight sat in her chest with the full mass of a thing that had been real and had mattered, and had not, until this moment, been allowed to matter all the way.
findings.Note: abstract telling-not-showing of emotional weight, circular phrasing that restates the beat's thesis rather than dramatizing it
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete physical/sensory detail of the memory's return

findings.Quote: Ekow stood in it like a man who'd stood in worse light waiting on worse people.
findings.Note: Vague tough-guy flourish that tells us Ekow's hardness rather than showing anything specific; reads as filler characterization.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical detail (a scar, a stance) that does specific work.

findings.Quote: He said it the way you state a logistical fact.
findings.Note: Explains the delivery instead of letting the dialogue itself carry the flat affect; slightly redundant telling.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause and let the terse dialogue speak for itself.

findings.Quote: They all smelled faintly of nothing, and nothing was its own smell.
findings.Note: Cute paradox that reads as a stylistic flourish rather than concrete observation; slightly undercuts the otherwise sharp sensory logic of the passage.
findings.Fix: Cut the second clause: 'They all smelled faintly of nothing.'

findings.Quote: Warmth was data too.
findings.Note: Aphoristic tag that tells us how to read the moment instead of trusting the scene.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let 'She let him have it' stand alone.

findings.Quote: A person who couldn't check the hour was a person who stayed.
findings.Note: Reads as a constructed maxim/aphorism rather than observed detail, slightly undercutting the otherwise concrete world-building.
findings.Fix: Fold into the concrete image rather than stating it as a rule, e.g. cut to the next paragraph's specifics.

findings.Quote: That was how trust worked in the gray zone. It was the most honest measure he had.
findings.Note: Explanatory aphorism telling the reader the meaning of the detail instead of letting the shrinking verification steps speak for itself.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence; let the fact stand.

findings.Quote: The Seam announced itself by what was missing. Which was correct. Which was what you wanted.
findings.Note: Fragmented sentences function as portentous authorial commentary/aphorism rather than sensory detail.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'The Seam announced itself by what was missing.'

findings.Quote: He ran nothing that ran him. He answered to the parcel and the clock and to no system at all.
findings.Note: Slides into aphoristic self-mythologizing that tells us Seto's independence thematically instead of trusting the preceding concrete detail (bearing repair, private map) to carry it.
findings.Fix: Cut or compress to a single concrete clause, e.g. 'He answered to the parcel and the clock.'

findings.Quote: as if the product had somewhere to be
findings.Note: Whimsical aside that reads as authorial wit rather than character-grounded observation.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause.

findings.Quote: A man does not land that close to a published maximum by accident. He had measured himself against a standard and chosen to live one millimeter inside it, every day, on purpose.
findings.Note: Aphoristic overexplanation of an already-clear detail; the second sentence just restates the first with added emphasis, slowing the beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence; let the millimeter detail stand alone.

findings.Quote: The suit was cut to be forgotten. That was the expensive part.
findings.Note: Neat aphoristic construction ('cut to be forgotten... that was the expensive part') reads as a stock cyberpunk-noir observation about wealth/anonymity rather than an organic perception.
findings.Fix: Ground it in one specific visual cue instead of the abstraction.

findings.Quote: the quiet of a building thinking about beginning
findings.Note: Purple personification that doesn't hold up literally — a building can't 'think about beginning' — and adds atmosphere without earning its cleverness given the beat's procedural tension.
findings.Fix: Cut to plain description: 'the quiet of the building before the shift changed.'

findings.Quote: the small metal complaint of a damper that had needed replacing since she moved into this desk
findings.Note: Mechanical detail is fine, but 'complaint' personifies the vent in a way that strains for texture rather than grounding time passage, slightly undercutting the clinical, controlled tone of the scene.
findings.Fix: Simplify to 'the small metal click of a damper that needed replacing.'

findings.Quote: It was two people keeping up a shared story about how things were going.
findings.Note: Aphoristic summary of the social dynamic that states the theme rather than dramatizing it further; slightly redundant after the preceding paragraph already showed this through her interior read of the conversation.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; the preceding lines already convey it.

findings.Quote: He sat with that the way he sat with a route that was bad in three places and was still the only route.
findings.Note: Abstract self-referential simile that doesn't clarify the emotional beat; slightly purple without adding concrete image.
findings.Fix: Trim to a plainer statement of the dilemma or ground the metaphor in a specific remembered route.

findings.Quote: the closures sitting there patient as a proof
findings.Note: Odd abstract simile ('patient as a proof') strains literal sense — proofs aren't patient — reads as reaching for profundity.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more literal description of the map's dead ends.

findings.Quote: He read it the way he read a street that had turned hostile with his back to it.
findings.Note: Purple simile that asserts a habitual reading skill without grounding it in anything established; slightly overwrought for the mechanical clarity of the rest of the passage.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with a concrete detail of how he actually reads it.

findings.Quote: closing the exits ahead of him, as if someone had drawn his most likely paths and unbuilt them one at a time
findings.Note: Doubles up on the 'hand clears a table' image immediately before it, restating the same idea in weaker abstract terms.
findings.Fix: Cut this clause; the table-clearing image already lands the point.

findings.Quote: The thought built there slowly, the way a route resolves out of a city you don't yet know — not whole, but turn by turn, until it holds.
findings.Note: Abstract, self-consciously literary aphorism about thinking that tells us he's realizing something without showing the content of the realization until the next paragraph; borders on filler-profundity.
findings.Fix: Cut or compress to a single concrete line, e.g. 'He worked it out slowly, one closure at a time.'

findings.Quote: a temperature that had been chosen by someone who would never have to live in it
findings.Note: Editorializing aphorism stapled onto the sensory description; tells us the class-critique instead of trusting the established detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause and let the preceding sensory list carry the point.

findings.Quote: she had spent seven years treating what she could verify as the same as what was true
findings.Note: Tidy thesis-statement of her complicity, verging on telling-not-showing the reframing the beat is supposed to dramatize through scene.
findings.Fix: Trim to something less aphoristic or move the insight later, earned by the Theodora scene.

findings.Quote: a stillness two mornings ago that hadn't matched anything he was doing, arriving in his chest with no source he could name
findings.Note: Vague interiority standing in for a precise sensation; 'arriving in his chest' is soft, unanchored phrasing.
findings.Fix: Specify a bodily or behavioral detail (missed beat, held breath, a task he stopped mid-motion) instead of naming the abstract feeling.

findings.Quote: a thing she was no longer allowed to set down, because she no longer remembered picking it up
findings.Note: reaches for poetic paradox but tips into stock sentimental phrasing

findings.Quote: like cupping water that wanted to run
findings.Note: the qualifier 'not literally, there was nothing to hold' undercuts the metaphor by over-explaining it
findings.Fix: trust the image, cut the meta-commentary clause

findings.Quote: held the intent steady the way you hold a heavy door with your shoulder while your hands are full
findings.Note: stock simile construction repeated from earlier beats' 'the way you...' pattern, diminishing impact through repetition

findings.Quote: heavier than the memory, and steadier
findings.Note: vague intensifier stacking ('heavier... steadier') reads as stock emotional shorthand rather than earned specificity
findings.Fix: anchor the decision in a concrete physical or procedural detail instead of comparative weight language

findings.Quote: She noticed it the way you notice a sound that stops — not when it goes wrong, but when it comes back to right.
findings.Note: neat aphoristic construction that explains the observation rather than letting the beacon detail land on its own; slightly pleased with its own cleverness
findings.Fix: trim to the observation itself without the generalized 'you notice' framing

findings.Quote: which made it worse
findings.Note: tells the reader the emotional valence directly instead of trusting the preceding detail (liking Yewande without complication) to carry it
findings.Fix: cut the trailing clause and let the prior sentence stand

findings.Quote: Somewhere three blocks from a checkpoint that no longer existed for him, a hand found a bicycle bell that wasn't there and pressed it twice, out of pure habit.
findings.Note: this bleed-in aside interrupts the beat's focus (Amara watching the broadcast) with an unrelated Seto image that isn't set up or paid off within this beat, diluting the intended payoff of her watching the announcement land
findings.Fix: cut or relocate this aside to a beat centered on Seto

findings.Quote: which was the thing she would remember later, that it did not feel like panic
findings.Note: Slightly clunky nested clause repeating 'did not feel like panic' awkwardly; mild telling-not-showing about the emotion's texture.
findings.Fix: Simplify to one clean clause, e.g., 'a clarity she would remember later as strange in its calm.'

findings.Quote: the way she'd read foot traffic herself, working the neuretics beat from a relay shop, clocking who came and went before a source showed
findings.Note: Comparison pulls focus onto her own backstory mid-tension beat, diluting the immediacy of Fonseca's suspicious behavior.
findings.Fix: Cut the comparison clause; let his behavior speak without the analogy.

findings.Quote: he'd left it running the way you leave a door open when you're not sure you're done going in and out of it
findings.Fix: cut the simile or replace with a concrete detail specific to the terminal/notice

findings.Quote: He'd saved for the gap like a bill he knew was coming. He hadn't saved for it being quiet.
findings.Note: the second sentence reaches for a neat aphoristic snap rather than landing an image
findings.Fix: cut second sentence or make it concrete (what 'quiet' actually costs him)

findings.Quote: the way you check a lock you already know is locked
findings.Note: stock comparative construction, slightly padding an otherwise sharp beat

findings.Quote: The logic wasn't missing. It was worse than missing. It was complete.
findings.Note: Aphoristic escalation that sounds punchy but doesn't add concrete information beyond restating certainty.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete inference about what the completeness implies for his next move.

findings.Quote: He didn't sleep. That wasn't unusual. The reason was.
findings.Note: Staccato reversal-hook opening is a familiar noir/thriller tic.
findings.Fix: Vary the rhythm so the hook doesn't lean on the stock three-beat construction.

findings.Quote: Three to four weeks wasn't a window. It was a decision.
findings.Note: aphoristic one-two punch that states the theme rather than dramatizing it

findings.Quote: The gap that had been a scheduling problem was turning into something he didn't have a name for yet.
findings.Note: tells the reader the emotional escalation instead of showing it via a concrete detail

findings.Quote: An object instead of a token. Objects made a moment feel considered instead of automated.
findings.Note: Redundant aphoristic doubling — states the same idea twice in abstract, telling rather than showing.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence; let the object stand without the explanatory gloss.

findings.Quote: Her eyes went to the blade before her mind had decided to look.
findings.Note: Stock 'body reacts before mind' formulation used often for danger/fear beats.
findings.Fix: Ground it in a more specific physical detail unique to Amara rather than the generic mind/body lag.

findings.Quote: just the two facts of skin arriving at the same temperature at the same t
findings.Note: the 'two facts of skin' phrasing strains for precision but lands as overwrought rather than grounded, especially cut off mid-word
findings.Fix: simplify to a plainer physical description of the contact
